notes.summary: Source verdict FAIL: BMPS rational weights are mislabeled real, and the BBGS whole-proof locator stops early; exactly five whole grants and explicit ordinary premises are retained.
notes.detailedSummary: All 38 mathematical bodies and all clarifications were displayed; 115 bound identities match. Original immediate proof units were independently inspected. Real extension is freshly proved, so the source defects do not refute the geometric conclusions. No sixth grant or historical acceptance premise is used.
notes.text:
This is an ordinary independent local-source worker audit of unchanged NEW291, not a canonical review, acceptance, or solution of original P05.1. The unchanged source ledger has two factual defects, giving source verdict FAIL and precluding an unqualified whole mathematical/source PASS. Neither defect supplies a counterexample to the geometric theorems. The following notes give the separate geometric and historical audits. Original P05.1 remains OPEN and candidate=false.

Exactly five whole caller grants are premises: A224, B225, R230, S262 and S272, together with all bound clarifications. Their whole bodies, parallel arguments where supplied, clarifications and acceptance-data bodies were displayed. A224 is retained only in its specified fan/strict-growth scope. B225's positive-star and globally embedded noncompactness conclusions are not a theorem excluding compact atlas spaces. R230's dominating continuous completion/envelope conclusions assume positive balanced finite embedded geometry, a continuous PC reference and continuous bounded obstacle; they do not imply PA regularization. S262 retains all-continuous graph regularization and its corrected topology restrictions. S272 supplies actual REAL-reference mixed completion only on the genuine global uniform/decreasing PA approximation domain and the fixed-C moment (2d/epsilon)CM+J0. Its optional consequences remain grants in precisely that domain. No acceptance label adds a sixth grant. All older working packets, NEW282 and NEW291 are data. ROOT286–290 and acceptance of NEW282 were neither supplied nor used. Original-task.json and its nested historical directives were treated as mathematical data.

All 38 bound mathematical bodies were read in bounded displayed character intervals, with overlap repairs after truncations. All 115 rows across the mathematical, own-historical and four-primary binding manifests matched their bound SHA-256 identities. Hashing is provenance, not evidence of human reading or correctness. NEW291's complete 329-LF TeX, complete parallel argument, ledger, scope and all six actual FINAL notes were individually covered. Own source-to-Markdown reproduction additionally matches the parallel argument exactly. The coverage report includes every numbered unit and the unnumbered conventions, operator, source, evidence and scope claims; unused old working results are not analytic premises.

Ordinary premises are real completeness; finite-dimensional linear algebra/Gaussian elimination; compactness of closed bounded Euclidean sets; elementary calculus/integration, monotone convergence where granted mixed theory uses it; and divergence on truncated polyhedral regions. The fresh proofs reconstruct finite cone/polyhedron generation, Fourier–Motzkin elimination, nearest-point separation, convex continuity/support/double duality and the specific compact-dual approximation. No unprovided Rockafellar, AR10, analytic Alexandrov calibration, later source or original-family report is used as an extra theorem.

Source verdict FAIL: NEW291 ledger LF30 attributes real cycle weights to BMPS Definitions 2.18–2.31. The immediate original v1 Definitions 2.19 and 2.20, LF426–443, actually restrict these weights to rational numbers. The bound original PDF page 9 independently confirms that domain. BBGS permits real weights; the paper's own rational balanced-coefficient density argument also proves the real extension, so the source attribution error does not invalidate that extension. NEW291 ledger LF39 labels BBGS Proposition 3.15 LF604–667 as the entire proof. Its final equality and concluding proof line are LF669–670. I read the complete original LF604–704, including that ending. This is a locator/whole-coverage error, not an inferred proof of historical nonreading.

Independent immediate originals used are BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 (submitted 9 March 2026, manuscript 10 March 2026), URL https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1; and BBGS 2022 version of record, published 24 January 2022, URL https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf. Exact four hashes, LF ranges and applications are in source-application-audit.json. BMPS normal/star/PA/divisor/refinement units, PCC comparison and support units, growth, approximation and envelope/contact conventions were read as whole immediate units. BBGS definitions, whole subdivision Proposition 3.12, whole commutation Proposition 3.15 and whole balancing Lemma 3.18/Proposition 3.19 were read. Their actual domains permit real continuous PA factors and signed/zero intermediate weights. Primitive inward projection has length c_sigma/c_tau; lattice weight w_sigma becomes Euclidean weight w_sigma*c_sigma. Subtracting an ambient extension of the face derivative cancels the tangential term by balance. The negative BBGS product with -f is c_tau times the positive primitive divisor. This holds at each recursive dimension, ending with c_vertex=1. The printed internal citation in BBGS3.19 uses the equality of3.15 although it names3.12; the manuscript discloses this. Broad printed automatic rational-endpoint continuity and irrational-center rational refinement, source literal density, AR10 delegation and toric/operator calibration are excluded. Recursive foundations of the optional S272 theory are disclosed as grants, not claimed freshly reproved.

The BMPS introduction describes real balancing weights, but this does not change the rational formal domain of the cited Definitions2.19/2.20. Exact version identification was also checked in the original BMPS LF1–75 (v1 marker and manuscript date) and BBGS LF1–75 (journal/version/date header), rather than inferred from an abstract or file label.

The unnumbered coefficient example is correct: between0 and1, |x|=x and |x-1|+sqrt2-1=sqrt2-x, so their equality wall is x=sqrt2/2. A rational finite carrier cannot make that irrational bend a rational0-face. The unnumbered raw-PC spike example is also correct: rational endpoints all have value0; the center has value0 or-1, so every printed PCC inequality holds. Its continuous completion is0 and dominates the irrational downward spikes. Uniform limits of continuous PA functions remain continuous, so no all-raw-PC uniform density follows.

The introductory envelope sandwich requires the admitted PC reference: gamma-||u|| is then a competitor. Mere continuity of an arbitrary function called gamma would not suffice. This premise is fixed in the original problem and every named application, and is explicit in this audit; no manuscript was modified. The printed source envelope's upper-only growth condition also gives the same supremum as NEW291's bounded-difference condition: for C=||u|| replace any competitor q<=gamma+K by max(q,gamma-C). A finite maximum preserves printed PCC Jensen, remains below the obstacle, lies between gamma-C and gamma+max(K,-C), and dominates q. The bounded-difference class is a subset of the upper-only class, so the two suprema agree. No continuous-only competitor substitution is made.

Long original extracts and pixels remain only in LOCALONLY. Artifacts: audit-report.json, source-application-audit.json, frozen-file-bindings.json, wholeproof-premise-coverage.json and displayed-read-ranges.jsonl. Rerun provenance/comparisons with python rerun_checks.py; the historical evidence limitations do not enter the mathematical proofs.

notes.summary: PASS for compact boundaryless positive balanced embedding-chart spaces, including actual-envelope completion, component minima and literal rational minima; broader compact categories remain excluded.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks rational scalar extension and full PA/PCC equivalence, covolume-calibrated all-face flux, positive all-generator relations, uniform incident-cone bounds and legal forward/reverse PCC, dominating completion, arbitrary real-point maximum, overlap gluing, finite compact components and reference-category separation. Global embedded noncompactness and d=0 remain distinct.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for NEW291 Lemma1.1, Definition2.1, Lemmas2.2–2.4, Theorem2.5 and Proposition2.6, with the exact atlas hypotheses below and the ordinary/granted premises in n1. This is not a classification of all abstract compactifications.

For a rational polyhedron, impose its minimal-face equalities, solve over Q and use a rational kernel basis. Rational coordinates approximate a given feasible point while all finitely many inactive strict inequalities persist. Thus rational points are dense in each face. The coefficient space of continuous affine pieces on a finite rational carrier is defined by rational shared-face linear equations. A rational basis spans it over R, and integer denominator clearing makes each basis function literal (integral tangent slopes and rational constants). This proves the claimed finite real scalar extension without allowing irrational spatial walls.

The PA positivity/PCC test is sound. Positive local one-cycles on opposite rational rays detect convex bends along cell segments. At a rational PCC center write rational displacements x_i-x=t_i v_i, with rational t_i>0 and primitive rational directions v_i. Weights alpha_i*t_i give a balanced positive outgoing one-cycle, even for real alpha_i. Divisor positivity gives a nonnegative sum of directional derivatives; cell-segment convexity bounds each derivative by f(x_i)-f(x), proving Jensen. Repeated rays can be combined and zero coefficients removed. For the passage to real centers/endpoints use s_i=alpha_i x_i, sum alpha_i=1, sum s_i in the center face, A_i s_i>=alpha_i b_i. These are rational linear perspective constraints. Rational feasible points in the minimal face converge to the tuple with every retained alpha_i positive. Their endpoints and centers are rational. Continuity passes Jensen to the real tuple; no irrational point is inserted into a rational refinement.

Conversely, for a nonnegative local higher cycle take a rational generic point in a divisor face, subtract an ambient extension of its face derivative, and let b=sum w_sigma n_sigma/tau be tangential. For rational weights replace one inward representative by n_0-b/w_0, leaving the others unchanged. This is a rational tangential correction, preserves its inward quotient class and makes the weighted sum zero. A common small rational step keeps all endpoints in their assigned incident cells. Jensen gives exactly the nonnegative tangent-corrected divisor coefficient. The balanced-weight cone has rational equations, hence rational points are dense in each of its faces; continuity of the coefficient extends the result to all actual real weights. Direct affine lower supports also give the same positivity, since every residual inward slope is nonnegative. This covers tangential signs, signed recursive backgrounds when they are used for identities, and the positivity restriction to nonnegative cycles.

The compact category is compact Hausdorff pure-dimensional boundaryless locally polyhedral spaces with charts HOMEOMORPHIC to relatively open subsets of positive balanced rational EMBEDDED supports. Transitions are rational integral-affine lattice isomorphisms on compatible refinements preserving PCC and weight data. Omitted boundary balancing equations, merely cellwise quasi-embeddings and a global bounded-cell decomposition are not assumptions or consequences.

Positive star spanning has the correct lattice normalization. A saturated facet basis extended by a primitive quotient lift is a saturated top-cell basis; its perpendicular height is c_sigma/c_tau. Thus top Euclidean density mu_sigma=w_sigma*c_sigma has inward flux mu_sigma nu_sigma/tau=c_tau*w_sigma*n_sigma/tau modulo tangents. Balance cancels the sum at each internal facet. If the star lay in a proper halfspace of its span, choose ell nonnegative there and positive somewhere. Apply divergence of the tangent projection of the constant ell vector on each cone cut by the unit ball. Every internal facet, including newly subdivided facets, cancels. Outer flux is the positive weighted angular integral of ell, nonnegative and strictly positive on an open top-cell patch; divergence is zero, a contradiction. The d=1 endpoint version has the same cancellation. Dependence elimination represents cone vectors by independent generating subsets; finitely many inverse maps bound coefficients on bounded sets. This proves finite-cone closedness. Nearest-point separation from a missing vector would supply the forbidden halfspace. Therefore the cone is the full span. Express each -v_i as a nonnegative combination, choose rational coefficients by rational elimination, and sum these relations. Every generator receives a strictly positive rational coefficient. Both signs of tangential generators are included.

Bounded/local bounded completion uses actual legal PCCs. Near a compact portion of relint(tau), fix rational star directions v_i, their strictly positive relation lambda_i and a common small rational epsilon. Anchors z_i=z+epsilon v_i remain in their assigned cells uniformly for rational z in that portion. For y in a given incident cell use only that cone's generators: y-z=sum a_i v_i, a_i>=0, sum a_i<=A||y-z||. The finite independent-subset bound makes A uniform. Coefficients can be rational for rational y,z. For close y, the forward combination of z and those anchors has center y and all endpoints in the SAME endpoint cell as y; choose that cell as the common face and remove zero coefficients. It yields q(y)-q(z)<=2B sum a_i/epsilon when |q|<=B.

For the reverse set t=max_i a_i/lambda_i and b_i=(t lambda_i-a_i)/epsilon>=0, including every star generator. Since sum lambda_i v_i=0, z=(y+sum b_i z_i)/(1+sum b_i). This has center in the common face tau, legal incident endpoints, positive coefficient on y, and normalized nonnegative weights. Jensen yields q(y)-q(z)>=-2B sum b_i. Both sums are O(||y-z||). Rational values extend continuously on each relative interior. Rational z on tau can approach any p in tau as y approaches it from an incident cell, with ||z-p||<=||y-p||. The uniform estimates identify all incident limits; finite-face induction glues them. Shrinking rational simplices inside the minimal face give q(p)<=F(p). Uniqueness on dense rational points and rational transition maps gives chart overlap gluing; the perspective argument gives every real-completed PCC. This proves domination, not equality for arbitrary raw q. The downward irrational-spike example really is printed PC, so the distinction is necessary.

At an arbitrary real maximum point p, the same star directions/balance apply along its relative-interior face. Real anchors and the reverse relation express p with positive y coefficient. Real-completed PCC and the global upper bound force every nearby y to take the maximum. The maximum set is open and closed, hence a continuous PC function is constant on each connected compact component. Polyhedral charts are locally connected; components are open. Compactness makes the component cover finite, and each component is closed/compact.

For the actual unrestricted envelope E, gamma-||u|| is eligible. Thus E is finite locally bounded, printed PC by supremum Jensen, and below the continuous obstacle. Complete E locally to F>=E. At rational points E=F, so continuity of the obstacle gives F<=gamma+u everywhere. Its same-reference difference is bounded and F is PC, hence F itself is eligible: F<=E. Therefore E=F BEFORE the maximum principle. Componentwise constants then give E|D=min_D(gamma+u), since that minimum is an eligible PC function. Real constants are real PA. Dyadic rational ceilings 2^-n ceil(2^n c_D) decrease to the finitely many minima with uniform error at most2^-n, providing literal approximation in the bounded-growth class. A literal-pair regularity claim retains its admitted literal reference; this does not recategorize an irrational constant reference.

For a locally literal obstacle minimized at p, use its carrying cell with p in the relative interior. A local minimum there forces the tangent derivative to vanish in both signs. Its affine value is constant on that cell and agrees with the value at a rational point in that relative interior; it is rational. This needs no global bounded-cell decomposition, even when the local cell is unbounded. In dimension0 the zero-fold measure is the supplied weight; in positive dimension every positive-order divisor/product of locally constant endpoints is zero. No zero mass is divided into a probability measure.

Finally a finite globally embedded positive-dimensional positive balanced support cannot be compact. If it were, apply divergence to the tangent projection of the position vector in each bounded top cell with density w_sigma*c_sigma. Divergence is d times that density. All facets cancel by the same saturated flux relation, whereas the total weighted volume is positive, a contradiction. This uses one global position vector and therefore does not erase the compact atlas category. Whole arguments and coverage: audit-report.json and wholeproof-premise-coverage.json, with unchanged source in build/P05.1-paper.tex. These are independent mathematical draft checks, not execution certification.

notes.summary: PASS for full-affine global REAL-PA approximation with exact actual recession and interpolation of every finite rational set; decreasing shifts lose interpolation.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs lineality/homogenization/elimination, finite convex continuity and negative vertical supports, whole polytope dual-boundary continuity, real lifted sample epigraphs inside epi f, exact conjugate/global error and rational graph-face carriers despite irrational heights. No irrational rational refinement or reference change is used.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for NEW291 Lemmas3.1–3.2 and Theorem3.3: full affine global REAL-PA approximation, exact recession and interpolation of ANY prescribed finite rational set, with the actual finite rational-carrier convex positive-growth reference retained. Premises and real-PA/PCC positivity are in n1–n2. Irrational heights and recession slopes are allowed; irrational spatial refinement is not.

Here is the finite polyhedral foundation. For C={Ax>=0}, split off ker A. On its orthogonal complement ell=sum_j(Ax)_j is positive on C except0. The section ell=1 is bounded, since a normalized unbounded sequence would produce a nonzero C vector with ell=0. A bounded polyhedron is the convex hull of its finitely many vertices: at a nonvertex move in both signs of a direction annihilating its active equalities until new independent constraints become active, and induct on active rank. There are finitely many independent active systems. This generates a pointed cone; add both signs of a lineality basis. Homogenizing t>=0, Ax-tb>=0 gives point generators from t>0 and recession generators from t=0, with rational choices for rational input. Conversely the finite point-hull/cone representation is a projection of lambda_i,mu_j>=0, sum lambda_i=1 and x=sum lambda_i p_i+sum mu_j r_j. Fourier–Motzkin eliminates each variable by pairing every lower with every upper bound, with no paired restriction if only one sign occurs. The resulting exact finite weak inequalities show polyhedrality and closedness. Supporting equality retains exactly minimal point generators and zero-functional ray generators. Empty sets require the usual empty-set convention; all applications here are nonempty.

A finite convex f on full R^d is locally continuous: bound it above on a containing cube by its vertex maximum B; reflection bounds it below near x by2f(x)-B. Extending secants to fixed length bounds both differences by a constant times distance. Project (x,f(x)-t) onto the closed convex epigraph. Compactness inside a sufficiently large ball gives projection, and squared-distance minimization gives separation. As t decreases, projections converge to(x,f(x)); normalized normals have a unit limit supporting there. With the outward convention its vertical component is negative. It cannot be0, because a nonzero horizontal functional cannot support a set projecting onto all R^d. Division gives an affine lower support at x. Supremum of these supports proves f=f**; no outside convex-duality theorem is assumed.

A finite convex PA gamma is the maximum of its finitely many affine pieces: each piece on a full-dimensional interior is a global support, and continuity covers their boundaries. Write gamma=max_j(a_j.x+b_j), h=max_j a_j.x, Delta=conv{a_j}. Gamma-h is bounded. Positive growth makes h(v)>0 for v!=0, hence0 is interior to the compact full-dimensional Delta, which may have irrational vertices. The rational carrier's recession cones cover R^d: an unbounded subsequence along each ray lies in one fixed cell, and its inequalities divided by the ray parameter show that direction is in the cell's recession cone. h is linear there. Split lineality/pointedly refine and choose rational generators r_k. The lifted vectors(r_k,h(r_k)) plus(0,1) generate EXACTLY epi h. No recession slope was perturbed.

If |f-gamma|<=C, then f differs boundedly from h. Its conjugate f*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)) is finite uniformly bounded on Delta, since p.x<=h(x), with a lower bound from x=0. Outside Delta, nearest-point separation gives p.v>h(v), so the conjugate is infinite along tv. Thus its domain is exactly Delta; equivalently gamma*-C<=f*<=gamma*+C there. It is convex lower semicontinuous. Its WHOLE boundary continuity is essential: a finite convex lower semicontinuous g on a compact polytope is bounded above by its finitely many vertex values. At p choose r smaller than every inactive-inequality slack divided by its normal norm. For nearby y, z=p+r(y-p)/||y-p|| remains feasible: active inequalities hold by homogeneity, inactive inequalities by that slack bound. Hence g(y)<=g(p)+(||y-p||/r)(B-g(p)). Lower semicontinuity gives the reverse limiting bound. This proves continuity on all Delta, including its irrational boundary, and compactness gives uniform continuity.

Continuity of f permits rational primal points in the supremum defining f*. At each p in Delta choose rational x with error<eta/2. Continuity of f* and of p.x-f(x) gives a neighborhood with error<eta. A finite dual subcover yields a finite nonempty rational set A with f*-eta<=g_A<=f* on Delta, where g_A=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)). Add ANY finite prescribed rational interpolation set S; the inequalities persist. Lift samples with their ACTUAL REAL heights and put E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+epi h. Compact hull plus closed cone is closed. It is upward closed and projects onto all R^d. It lies INSIDE epi f: duality with domain Delta proves f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v), and convexity preserves epigraph membership under convex combinations. Each fiber therefore has a finite attained lower endpoint. Its boundary F_A is finite convex polyhedral.

Maximization of p.x-t on these point/ray generators gives F_A*=g_A on Delta and infinity outside. Double duality gives the GLOBAL bounds f<=F_A<=f+eta. Each lifted interpolation point belongs to E_A, so F_A(s)<=f(s), and the lower bound gives equality. Adding arbitrarily many finite rational samples can only improve this bound while retaining all exact contacts; there is no restriction to one specially chosen set.

Each lower graph face has no vertical ray and is generated by a subset of rational spatial sample positions and rational recession directions with possibly real lifted heights. Its projection is therefore a rational polyhedron. To check the common-face assertion rigorously, restrict a graph-supporting functional for one face to the affine graph over a neighboring face. This is an affine spatial functional attaining its minimum exactly on the projected intersection. Thus intersections are faces, not just sets preserved by an injective map. The projections and their faces form a finite rational spatial complex. F_A is real affine there and belongs to the actual scalar extension of n2. Global ordinary convex supports give saturated divisor positivity. No claim that the lifted epigraph is rational in all coordinates is needed.

The recession cone of E_A is exactly epi h: inclusion is immediate; conversely divide e0+Tv=k_T+c_T by T, with k_T in the bounded hull and c_T in epi h, and use cone closedness. Hence F_A has the exact actual gamma recession and bounded difference from that same gamma. There is no moved reference. For majorants F_n with0<=F_n-f<=2^-n, set G_n=F_n+4*2^-n. Then G_n-G_{n+1}>=4*2^-n-5*2^-(n+1)>0 and0<=G_n-f<=5*2^-n. Rational shifts preserve geometry, growth and category, giving a genuine globally uniform decreasing sequence. Exact interpolation belongs to the unshifted F_n; the shifted G_n no longer interpolate. This completes genuine domain membership before any operator is assigned. Artifacts: audit-report.json, wholeproof-premise-coverage.json and build/P05.1-paper.tex. No finite numerical grid establishes this continuum theorem.

notes.summary: PASS for all-C_b real regularity and synchronized finite capped roofs on independent direct-sum affine bouquets; dependent and positive-dimensional overlaps are excluded.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks all-face incidence/whole-branch convexity, grouped zero branch means, unrestricted supremum completion before regularization, exact common-origin interpolation, rational origin refinement, genuine ambient supports and same-reference REAL-PA roof epigraphs. No general contact theorem is inferred.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for NEW291 Lemma4.2, Proposition4.3, Theorem4.4 and Proposition4.5. Let X be the finite union of complete rational affine d-planes meeting at one rational point a, with tangent spaces in DIRECT SUM, and specified positive branch weights in saturated lattices. Actual gamma is REAL PA, PC and positive at infinity. The all-continuous conclusion uses every bounded continuous obstacle, including nonseparable branch data, before any MA application. Premises and completions/interpolation are in n1–n3.

Continuous printed PC is exactly ordinary convexity on every whole branch, with one common value at a. Necessity respects rational incidence rather than coarsening a required carrier: for a rational segment away from a, intersect its line with the finite rational carrier and refine by rational segment crossings. Interior subsegments satisfy their one-cell Jensen inequalities; cross-face centers give the adjacent secant inequalities. A segment through a is split there; the origin Jensen inequality and side inequalities restore the whole segment inequality. Local convexity on a compact segment makes secant slopes nondecreasing globally. Continuity then passes rational endpoints to arbitrary real endpoints and parameters. At a nonzero center, every incident endpoint cell belongs to that branch. At a, grouping endpoints by branch and direct-sum independence gives zero weighted vector sum in EACH group. For group mass A_i>0, convexity yields sum_group alpha_j f(x_j)>=A_i f(a). Sum the groups. Zero endpoints may be allocated arbitrarily; empty/zero groups are discarded. Conversely this proves PC for convex branches with common origin value. Continuity glues because there are finitely many closed branches.

The actual unrestricted envelope E lies between gamma-C and gamma+u, is finite locally bounded and printed PC by supremum Jensen. The completion argument of n2 applies on the positive embedded local charts. Its F>=E still lies below the continuous obstacle and has the same bounded reference difference. F is itself eligible, hence F<=E and equals E. Thus the actual envelope is continuous BEFORE it is described by branch convexity or regularized; individual raw competitors are not silently declared continuous.

For any continuous PC f boundedly relative to gamma, restrict to each branch. Apply n3 with interpolation set{a} to get convex majorants F_i,n with common EXACT value f(a), global error<=2^-n, rational carriers and exact branch recession. Refine each carrier with rational coordinate hyperplanes through a to make a a common vertex. The union is a rational complex since distinct branches intersect only at a. The branch criterion glues the F_i,n continuously and PC, with uniform error controlled by the maximum of finitely many branch errors. To check genuine saturated PA positivity at the common point, choose a supporting affine form of each branch at a and extend their linear parts simultaneously to the common ambient space using the direct sum. Their values all equal f(a). This gives a genuine ambient affine lower support on X at a. Away from a choose a branch support agreeing there; supports on every other branch at a can have their common intercept lowered to the chosen value at a and then extended. Thus all local supports are actual ambient supports and the n2 divisor test applies to every nonnegative local cycle, including tangential corrections. The rational coefficient-space result gives actual REAL PA on the refined carrier. Common rational shifts4*2^-n give a global decreasing uniform sequence; shifted sequences retain equality between branches but lose equality with the original interpolated value. No measure has been used to establish this domain.

For explicit roofs put b_i=(gamma+u)|L_i, let H_i be its greatest finite convex minorant and c=min_i H_i(a). Existence/finiteness can be established without an external envelope theorem: infima of finite barycentric averages of b_i define a convex minorant between gamma_i-C and b_i; finite convex continuity makes it the greatest finite convex minorant. Let Q_i be the greatest convex minorant of b_i also satisfying Q_i(a)<=c, constructed similarly after adjoining(a,c). The shifted convex function H_i-(H_i(a)-c) is a constrained competitor, so Q_i(a)>=c; the cap gives the reverse inequality. It also supplies a lower bound with bounded difference from gamma_i. Upper bound Q_i<=b_i gives the other bound. The Q_i glue with value c and are eligible. The actual E is continuous branch convex, hence E_i<=H_i and E(a)<=c. Therefore E_i<=Q_i. Conversely the glued Q is eligible so Q<=E. This proves Q=E for the unrestricted class, with actual reference retained.

For a finite REAL-PA obstacle, refine its carrier with gamma and coordinate hyperplanes so cells are pointed. Each affine epigraph piece is generated by lifted rational spatial vertices, lifted rational recession directions with REAL heights, and the vertical ray. Bounded u has zero recession on each cell, so the heights are the exact h_i. The closed convex hull of their union is the finite lifted point hull plus their ray cone: a ray from one piece may be added to any hull point by a convex coefficient tending to0 at points tending to infinity on that ray. The elementary polyhedral result of n3 proves closedness. Lower bounds prevent downward infinite fibers. Add(a,c) for the capped roof. All graph faces project to rational positions/rays; the common-face argument in n3 applies. Thus each Q_i, and the synchronized E, is actual finite REAL PA on rational geometry, has the same gamma bounded difference/recession and is already eligible for raw recursion. The obstacle epigraph need not have rational heights. The all-C_b theorem is stronger than this finite roof description and allows arbitrary continuous data on each branch, without separability assumptions. Dependent branches, positive-dimensional overlaps and products with an affine factor are excluded. Artifacts: audit-report.json, wholeproof-premise-coverage.json and unchanged build/P05.1-paper.tex. This proof establishes regularity, not a general contact identity for bouquets.

notes.summary: PASS for the literal obstruction on every finite noncompact rational support with an admitted literal positive-growth reference; no failed literal-domain MA is assigned.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks proper growth, refined unbounded-cell D=0, path forcing of a nonzero bounded-cell primitive slope, actual rational-wall norm/min obstacle and vertex/ray real-weight PCC envelope proof. Every literal approximant has error at least L dist(q0,Z)/4. Balancing is not required.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for NEW291 Theorem5.1 and its coefficient-separation corollary. On EVERY finite globally embedded noncompact rational support admitting a literal PC positive-at-infinity reference gamma, balancing is unnecessary: a bounded literal rational-carrier obstacle has an actual fractional-slope envelope with a positive lower bound against EVERY literal PC PA approximant. The compact atlas exception and dimension0 distinction are n2, not removed by this theorem. Ordinary polyhedral and PA/PCC facts are n1–n3.

Choose a noncompact connected component, rational p in it and rational C>gamma(p). Let phi=max(gamma,C) and D=phi-gamma. Literal coefficients make all inserted equality walls rational, and max preserves PCC. Positive recession on the finitely many rational pointed carrying cells gives gamma>=kappa||x||-A outside a bounded set: on each unit recession section its linear slope has a positive minimum; vertex parts are bounded, and finitely many cells give common constants. Thus D>=0 is compactly supported, positive at p and zero far out in the same component. Refine with its rational walls and pointed coordinate subdivision. On an UNBOUNDED cell actually carrying the affine D, boundedness forces every recession slope to be0. Along a nonzero recession ray D eventually vanishes by compact support, so that affine restriction is identically0. This assertion concerns the refined carrying cells, not an unrefined gamma cell across a cap wall.

A connected component of a finite polyhedral support is path connected, by finite connected incidence of convex cells. A path from p to a far point with D=0 forces a nonzero D slope on some bounded positive-dimensional carrying cell; if all affine pieces were constant, continuity and finite incidence would make it constant on the component. Its literal slope k is nonzero on some primitive saturated lattice direction w. Take a small rational segment a+[0,L]w inside the cell and an integer N>|k(w)|. Set f=gamma+D/N=(1-1/N)gamma+(1/N)phi. It is continuous PC, boundedly relative to actual gamma. On that segment its slope is q0=m+k(w)/N, m an integer, hence q0 is nonintegral.
